source_state: Uncommitted tank-driving work plus the ordinary-match footing controller; code identities below.
notes: Playable CPU footing is enabled for both tanks; headless defaults retain the old range-only CPU for comparisons.
Accepted wheel torque 300 and motor damping 240, suspension, support rules, range policy, aim and shot timing are unchanged.
Forks copy the native physics world and both existing controllers. Only the selected player enables footing; the opponent retains the old range policy.
Final traces contain twelve old-policy controls, eighteen enabled full matches and two frozen comparisons; intermediate tuning/exploration runs in the temporary directory are excluded.
All twelve controls reproduce observations captured before adding the footing policy. The final source with footing disabled reproduces that retained behavior.
Current source moves driving_lab/goal.rs and its tests to driving/goal.rs. Apply the final overlay to the base revision; applying over the before overlay also requires removing the listed old paths.
Completion requires actual support, both wheel contacts for sprung tanks, improved tilt and low linear/angular velocity. Terrain estimates alone do not complete goals.
One Round seed-99 goal is blocked by changing terrain before the fight ends. There is no general route-finding or win-rate claim; later enemy fire can change a completed footing.
Mode counts stop at the first death; fixed-duration traces continue afterward. Do not treat post-death motion as gameplay evidence.
Benchmarks ran serially after compilation and before opening the GUI. Timings are single desktop samples of different combat workloads, not isolated controller overhead.
Source/native overlays under /tmp are local archives; repository traces retain observations/controller histories and reproduction commands. Commands recreate the native captures.
